title: JGB Yields Trend: 2026 Outlook
abstract: A quiet shift in Tokyo's bond market is forcing global funds to rethink their hedging playbook for the year ahead.
body:
## JGB Yields Trend: 2026 Outlook

On 2026-04-12, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield closed at 1.42 percent, its highest since 2011, according to data from the Japan Bond Trading Co. The move extends a 14-month repricing that has caught many global fixed-income desks off guard. Nomura chief rates strategist Akira Tanaka said in a note dated 2026-04-10 that the market is now pricing a terminal policy rate of 1.25 percent by March 2027, up from 0.75 percent in January.

The shift is not a sudden spike. It is the cumulative result of three forces: a slow normalization by the Bank of Japan, a widening domestic inflation impulse, and a retreat by the world's largest bond investors. Each has its own timeline, and together they are rewriting the playbook for yen hedgers and global funds.

## The BoJ's Quiet Normalization

The Bank of Japan ended its yield curve control program in March 2024, then raised its policy rate twice in 2025. At the January 2026 meeting, the board voted 7-2 to lift the uncollateralized overnight call rate to 0.75 percent. Governor Kazuo Ueda told reporters that the bank would proceed "without preconceptions," a phrase that traders now parse for hints of a faster pace.

Since then, the BoJ has reduced its monthly purchases of 5- to 10-year JGBs to 2.4 trillion yen from 4.0 trillion yen a year earlier. The central bank still holds roughly 53 percent of the outstanding JGB market, but the marginal buyer is stepping back. That matters because the BoJ was the price-insensitive bid for a decade. Without it, yields must clear at levels that attract private investors.

Tanaka of Nomura estimates that the "fair value" for the 10-year yield, based on current inflation and growth expectations, is between 1.30 and 1.55 percent. The market is now testing the upper end of that range. He expects the BoJ to raise the policy rate once more in July 2026, to 1.00 percent, and again in January 2027, to 1.25 percent.

## Inflation That Sticks

Japan's core consumer price index, which excludes fresh food, rose 2.4 percent year on year in February 2026, the 35th consecutive month above the BoJ's 2 percent target. Services inflation, a key gauge of domestic price pressure, was 2.1 percent. Wage growth has followed. The annual shunto wage negotiations concluded in March 2026 with an average base pay increase of 3.6 percent, according to the Japanese Trade Union Confederation, the third straight year above 3 percent.

Mizuho chief economist Yumi Sato argues that this is no longer a cost-push story driven by energy imports. "The inflation is now domestic and broad," she wrote on 2026-04-08. "Firms are passing on labor costs, and households are accepting higher prices because wages are rising too." Sato forecasts core CPI will average 2.2 percent in fiscal 2026, well above the BoJ's 1.8 percent projection.

That gap between market and central bank forecasts is why the long end of the curve has steepened. The 30-year yield touched 2.35 percent on 2026-04-11, a level last seen in 2008. Life insurers and pension funds, the traditional buyers of super-long debt, have been slow to return. They are waiting for even higher yields, according to a survey by the Life Insurance Association of Japan published on 2026-04-05.

## Global Funds Retreat

The third force is external. Foreign investors sold a net 4.2 trillion yen of Japanese bonds in the first quarter of 2026, the largest quarterly outflow since 2013, according to Ministry of Finance data released on 2026-04-08. The selling was concentrated in short and medium maturities, where hedging costs have become prohibitive.

The three-month yen-dollar basis swap widened to minus 55 basis points on 2026-04-09, from minus 30 basis points in December 2025. For a European or US investor, the cost of hedging yen exposure now exceeds the yield pickup on most JGBs. That has forced a rethink. "We have moved from a duration trade to a currency trade," said Henrik Larsen, head of global rates at Nordea Asset Management, on 2026-04-07. "If you cannot hedge the yen, you do not buy the bond."

Some funds are instead buying Japanese equities or direct real estate, where the currency exposure is unhedged but the expected return is higher. Others are simply staying away. The result is a buyer's strike at the short end, even as domestic institutions slowly return to the long end.

## What to Watch

The next inflection point is the BoJ's quarterly outlook report, due on 2026-04-28. If the board raises its inflation forecast for fiscal 2026 above 2 percent, traders will price a faster pace of hikes. Tanaka of Nomura says a move to 1.00 percent in June, rather than July, is possible if the yen weakens past 155 per dollar. The currency traded at 152.30 on 2026-04-12.

A second risk is the global term premium. If US Treasury yields rise further, JGB yields will follow, even without a BoJ move. The 10-year US Treasury yield was 4.35 percent on 2026-04-11. The correlation between US and Japanese 10-year yields has been 0.78 over the past six months, according to Bloomberg data.

For now, the trend is clear. The era of zero percent JGB yields is over. The market is slowly, unevenly, and sometimes painfully finding a new equilibrium. As Sato of Mizuho put it on 2026-04-08: "The destination is not in doubt. Only the speed is."
